issues.legal_issue: A tenant's acquisition of vacant possession of an owned residence after the tenancy begins establishes the alternative-residence ground for eviction even if the tenant no longer possesses that residence when the eviction petition is filed.
material_facts: The tenant owned another residence, and its previous occupant handed over vacant possession to her after the rented premises had been let to her.
The tenant sold the residence four days after obtaining possession.
The tribunal found no oral agreement to sell the residence before it became vacant, so it was available to the tenant for occupation when possession was obtained.
The tenant no longer possessed the residence when the eviction petition was filed.
issues.conclusion: The tenant's subsequent loss of possession before the eviction petition was filed did not protect her from eviction under Section 14(1)(h) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1)(h) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, obtaining vacant possession of another residence that is available for the tenant's occupation after the tenancy begins establishes the eviction ground. The tenant's later loss of possession, including before the eviction petition is filed, does not defeat that ground. The High Court had endorsed the view in Hem Chand Baid v. Smt. Prem Wati Parekh, AIR 1980 Delhi 1; the Supreme Court applied the statutory ground to the facts here.

predicates.proceeding_under_alternative_residence_e: An eviction proceeding was brought on the basis that the tenant had acquired vacant possession of another residence.
predicates.tenant_owned_residence_became_vacant: A residence owned by the tenant became vacant and the tenant obtained possession of it after the rented premises had been let.
predicates.residence_available_for_tenant_occupatio: When the tenant obtained possession, the residence was available for the tenant to occupy and was not subject to a previously established obligation preventing that occupation.
predicates.alternative_residence_eviction_ground_is: The statutory ground for eviction based on the tenant's acquisition of another residence is established.

issues.definition: If an eviction proceeding rests on the tenant acquiring another residence and the tenant obtains vacant possession of an owned residence that is available for occupation after the tenancy begins, the alternative-residence eviction ground is established.
